newsitem.title: USA: U.S. cash crudes down but off lows on Cano Limon.
newsitem.headline: U.S. cash crudes down but off lows on Cano Limon.

text.p: U.S. cash crude prices remained depressed early Thursday afternoon but off the day's lows, with West Texas Sour/Midland (WTS) and other grades getting brief respite from news that production was shut-in at Occidental Petroleum Corp's Cano Limon field after a rebel bomb.
Benchmark West Texas Intermediate/Cushing (WTI) was down around five to 10 cents early afternoon at about $19.30/35 a barrel, compared with a low around $19.10.
WTS traded down at $1.35 under WTI Thursday mid-morning, matching Wednesday's lowest level. It bounced back a few cents after the Cano Limon news but was drifting lower
Eugene Island followed WTS lower and was at $1.55/$1.50 under WTI before edging back to $1.50/$1.45. It traded at $1.46 and $1.45 below, traders said.
"It (WTS) was very overheated anyway and it should be back out below $2 (discount)," said a trader for a medium-sized integrated oil company.
"Sour is at a standstill right now," said a trader for a major oil company.
Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James (LLS) was showing signs of easing after trading at 21 cents over WTI, down from levels around 25 cents over on Wednesday, traders said.
"People thought 21 looked like a good number and it looks like it's run out of steam," said a major oil company trader.
LLS has improved from a 25 cent discount to WTI in the past month, mainly due to the closed arbitrage and prospect of few North Sea Brent barrels in the weeks ahead.
Heavy Louisiana Sweet/Empire was quoted at 35/30 cents discount, though there wasn't much trading interest, traders said.
